ui.about.credits_text: Timeline parsing, projection and camera framing build on Google Timeline Visualizer by mahlernim (MIT). Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, basemaps © CARTO. Video encoding by FFmpeg. Interface built with Qt for Python. Fonts: Outfit and Instrument Sans (SIL OFL), DejaVu.
ui.about.detail.camera: Plans every frame of the camera: zoom style, framing on arrival, time per trip and a final pass that evens out on-screen speed. The result is smooth by construction and checked for jerk.
ui.about.detail.encode: FFmpeg encodes the segments with the fastest encoder that passed a real test on this computer (NVIDIA, Intel, AMD or software). Any fallback is shown and needs your consent.
ui.about.detail.frames: Draws each frame: graded map, travelled route, glowing recent trail, the marker (a plane on flights), titles and an optional motion blur. Frames are written in segments so an interrupted render resumes where it stopped.
ui.about.detail.import: Reads Timeline.json, location-history.json, old Records.json exports and Takeout ZIPs as a stream, so even very large files stay within memory. Visits, movements and their transport mode (walking, motorbike, car, train, ferry, flight) are kept.
ui.about.detail.journey: Selects the period, removes GPS teleport spikes and splits the route into local episodes and long trips. Flights become arcs.
ui.about.detail.preview: Runs the exact same engine at a smaller size so you can scrub through the video and pin Director's Cut keyframes before rendering.
ui.about.detail.repair: If a file is damaged, every problem is listed with a confidence level (high, medium, low) before anything changes. Fixes go into a new file with a report; your original is never touched.
ui.about.detail.tiles: Downloads only the map tiles the camera will show (CARTO with your API key, or your own offline MBTiles), caches them and applies the theme's colour grade once per tile.
ui.about.detail.verify: The finished MP4 is checked (size, frame rate, frame count, audio, decodability) before it appears in your Video Library with a thumbnail.
ui.about.flow_note: Click a stage (or use the arrow keys) to see what happens there. Dashed stages are optional.
ui.about.optional: Optional stage · runs on this computer.
ui.about.privacy: No account, no upload, no telemetry. Your Timeline file is read locally and never modified; only map tiles are downloaded.
ui.about.subtitle: What the app is, how it works, and who made it.

ui.camera.framing.balanced.desc: After a long trip, the camera settles in on the area you arrive in.
ui.camera.framing.close.desc: Settles in tighter on arrival, for more street-level detail.
ui.camera.framing.off.desc: Keep the zoom style's framing when you arrive somewhere.
ui.camera.keyframes_note: Manual camera positions blended into the automatic path with the same easing. Add them from the Preview page at the current frame.
ui.camera.ltp.balanced.desc: Long trips move a little quicker, leaving more time for local moments.
ui.camera.ltp.faster.desc: Long trips are brisk; most of the video goes to what you did there.
ui.camera.ltp.fastest.desc: Long trips become quick links between chapters — still animated, never a jump cut.
ui.camera.ltp.natural.desc: Long trips get the time their on-screen motion needs.
ui.camera.moved_note: Zoom style, long-trip detection, local trip framing and long-trip pacing are set in Journey Builder.
ui.camera.zoom.active.desc: Zooms in on local movement and pulls out for long trips. The recommended default.
ui.camera.zoom.balanced.desc: Shows more of the surrounding geography with gentle zoom changes. Best for trips across regions.
ui.camera.zoom.close_up.desc: Stays as close to you as possible. Best for city life and daily routes.
ui.camera.zoom.fixed.desc: One zoom level for the whole video. Calm and map-like; best for short routes.
ui.dashboard.env_disclaimer: Capacity information is measured; the recommendation is an estimate, not a performance guarantee.
ui.dashboard.ffmpeg_missing: FFmpeg was not found. Rendering needs FFmpeg.
ui.dashboard.no_hw: No hardware video encoder passed its test encode. Software encoding (x264/x265) will be used; it is slower but produces equivalent quality.
ui.dashboard.scanning: Scanning this computer (CPU, memory, GPU, FFmpeg)…

ui.import.privacy: The file is read locally and never modified. Large files are parsed incrementally and can resume if interrupted.
ui.import.reversed: The export was newest-first; it was read in chronological order.

ui.journey.trips.conservative.desc: Only clearly long hops count as long trips, so the camera pulls out less often.
ui.journey.trips.sensitive.desc: Shorter intercity hops count too: more overview shots between places.

ui.video.hires_continue: You can still continue — nothing will be downscaled automatically.

ui.video.hires_nohw: No verified hardware encoder: software encoding at this size is slow.
ui.video.hires_ram: This computer has {gb} GB of RAM; 16 GB or more is recommended.
ui.video.hires_vram: Detected VRAM is {mb} MB; hardware encoding may be unavailable at this size.
ui.video.hires_warn: High resolution: expect long render times and about {mb} MB of temporary disk space.
ui.video.motion_blur_note: Film-style 180° shutter: fast pans and flights blur like a real camera instead of stepping. Frames with motion are rendered 2–6 times and averaged, so rendering takes roughly 2–4× longer. Preview stays sharp.
